question: Does a real stage failure stay diagnosable from stdout alone, without opening the stage log file?
method: Temporarily inserted one line - throw "ISSUE-284-MANUAL-BREAK: ..." - into scripts/verify.ps1's own 'sim' stage body, right after all three Invoke-Scenario calls and Assert-FilesEqual had already succeeded and routed their own output to the stage log file, so the failure happens after real content had already accumulated for that stage.
Ran the mutated verify.ps1 with -Stage sim and a real Godot path (sim needs the engine per PR #289's gate, for the NuGet profile, even though its own body never calls the engine directly).
Captured full stdout+stderr to a file and confirmed a non-zero exit code.
Reverted the injected line with 'git checkout -- scripts/verify.ps1' immediately after capturing the output below; the line never reached a commit.
command: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify.ps1 -Stage sim -GodotPath "C:/gamedev/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64_console.exe" -TemporaryRoot C:\gdftmp284 > real-break-demo.log 2>&1
finding: stdout alone shows: the failed stage name and how many lines its log holds; the last 20 lines of that stage's own captured output (dotnet restore/build text and all three scenario_result events with checksums - exactly the context leading up to the failure); and the final verification_result with failedPhase, failedStage and the exception reason. The trailing PowerShell error-record block (garbled Cyrillic in this capture) is powershell.exe's own default uncaught-exception formatting, not something this change added or controls, and the OEM/UTF-8 codepage mismatch that garbles it is a pre-existing property of this shell, unrelated to Issue #284. None of the diagnostic content required opening the log file at .artifacts/verify-4c5f2527d48a4c988971f7fd88b90175/stage-output.log, which the run's best-effort cleanup had already deleted by the time this capture was reviewed.
